\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أهمية} (ahammiyya)}{أهمية (ahammiyya)}]{\ar{أهمية} (ahammiyya) — importance}

\label{lesson:AR-C368-ahammiyya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for awareness, then the Arabic for knowledge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أهمية}}
\textbf{\ar{أهمية}} — \emph{ahammiyya} — \textquotedblleft{}importance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يعرف} \ar{الجميع} \ar{أهمية} \ar{النوم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yaʿrifu al-jamīʿ ahammiyyat an-nawm.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Everyone knows the importance of sleep.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أهمية}} (\emph{ahammiyya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{h-m-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to concern, to trouble\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Ahammiyya} is a modern abstract noun from \emph{ahamm}, more important: importance.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ahammiyya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ahammiyya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yaʿrifu al-jamīʿ ahammiyyat an-nawm.} — Everyone knows the importance of sleep.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for awareness, then the Arabic for knowledge, then say \emph{ahammiyya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أهمية} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Importance\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{قيمة} (qīma)}{قيمة (qīma)}]{\ar{قيمة} (qīma) — a value}

\label{lesson:AR-C368-qima}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for knowledge, then the Arabic for importance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{قيمة}}
\textbf{\ar{قيمة}} — \emph{qīma} — \textquotedblleft{}a value\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{هذه} \ar{الساعة} \ar{لها} \ar{قيمة} \ar{كبيرة} \ar{عندي}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hādhihi as-sāʿa lahā qīma kabīra ʿindī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This watch has great value for me.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{قيمة}} (\emph{qīma}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-w-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to stand, to rise\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A \emph{qīma} is what a thing stands at: its worth, its value.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qīma}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hādhihi as-sāʿa lahā qīma kabīra ʿindī.} — This watch has great value for me.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for knowledge, then the Arabic for importance, then say \emph{qīma} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ركز} (rakkaza)}{ركز (rakkaza)}]{\ar{ركز} (rakkaza) — to focus}

\label{lesson:AR-C368-rakkaza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for importance, then the Arabic for a value.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ركز}}
\textbf{\ar{ركز}} — \emph{rakkaza} — \textquotedblleft{}to focus\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ركز} \ar{الطالب} \ar{على} \ar{دروسه}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rakkaza aṭ-ṭālib ʿalā durūsih.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The student focused on his lessons.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يركز}, \emph{yurakkiz}.

It takes \ar{على}: \ar{ركز} \ar{على} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ركز}} (\emph{rakkaza}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-k-z}, \textquotedblleft{}to fix firmly in the ground\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, to plant firmly: to fix the mind on one thing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rakkaza}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rakkaza}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rakkaza aṭ-ṭālib ʿalā durūsih.} — The student focused on his lessons.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for importance, then the Arabic for a value, then say \emph{rakkaza} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أهمل} (ahmala)}{أهمل (ahmala)}]{\ar{أهمل} (ahmala) — to neglect}

\label{lesson:AR-C368-ahmala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a value, then the Arabic for to focus.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أهمل}}
\textbf{\ar{أهمل}} — \emph{ahmala} — \textquotedblleft{}to neglect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أهمل} \ar{الرجل} \ar{حديقته} \ar{فماتت} \ar{الزهور}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ahmala ar-rajul ḥadīqatahu fa-mātat az-zuhūr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The man neglected his garden, so the flowers died.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يهمل}, \emph{yuhmil}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أهمل}} (\emph{ahmala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{h-m-l}, whose Form I Lane gives for water overflowing (Lane). Form IV is to leave cattle to graze with no herdsman, and so to leave a thing to itself: to neglect.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ahmala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ahmala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ahmala ar-rajul ḥadīqatahu fa-mātat az-zuhūr.} — The man neglected his garden, so the flowers died.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a value, then the Arabic for to focus, then say \emph{ahmala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أهمل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To neglect\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اهتم} (ihtamma)}{اهتم (ihtamma)}]{\ar{اهتم} (ihtamma) — to care about}

\label{lesson:AR-C368-ihtamma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to focus, then the Arabic for to neglect.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اهتم}}
\textbf{\ar{اهتم}} — \emph{ihtamma} — \textquotedblleft{}to care about\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تهتم} \ar{أختي} \ar{بالموسيقى}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tahtammu ukhtī bi-l-mūsīqā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister cares about music.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يهتم}, \emph{yahtamm}.

It takes \ar{بـ}: \ar{اهتم} \ar{بـ} …. The noun \ar{اهتمام} is interest.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اهتم}} (\emph{ihtamma}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{h-m-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to concern, to trouble\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VIII, to be concerned for: to care about.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ihtamma}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ihtamma}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tahtammu ukhtī bi-l-mūsīqā.} — My sister cares about music.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to focus, then the Arabic for to neglect, then say \emph{ihtamma} again
\end{itemize}
